question: Does the closed-cohort feedback barrier explain delayed-feedback learning throughput, and how does increasing the existing batch size affect liveness and harmful exposure?
scope: Synthetic diagnostic and batch-size sensitivity using production controller and TS. No product defaults or quality/pending gates are changed. Historical v2 results for seeds 0..15 have already been inspected.
fixed_constraints: Default prior, posterior draws, minimum-family and promotion thresholds
Four pending candidates and 200 total trial candidates
Sticky assignment, closed-cohort publication, revised-label replacement, rollback and monitoring semantics
Paired potential outcomes for each scenario and seed; no access to unselected potential outcomes by the learner
analysis: Attribute unenrolled baseline arrivals to closed-cohort feedback/reconciliation waits or other guards.
Inspect decision-time family counts, incomplete counts, posterior probability and allocation.
Report adoption within the workload separately from adoption during feedback drain.
Compare harmful trial/deployment exposure in harmful and long-revision scenarios; no favorable-only selection.
A positive synthetic result does not establish correctness under real judge errors or justify changing a product default by itself.
